cohort: 161,471 healthy, term, singleton neonates born at ≥36 weeks' gestation between 2009 and 2013 from 14 Kaiser Permanente Northern California hospitals, with a subset of 7075 newborns (4525 vaginal delivery, 2550 cesarean delivery) who were exclusively formula-fed
finding: Nomograms depicting percentiles of weight loss by hour of age were developed for both vaginally and cesarean-delivered newborns who are exclusively formula fed, demonstrating that weight loss >7% was rare after vaginal delivery and weight loss >8% was rare after cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean-delivered neonates had higher median weight loss at 48 and 72 hours compared to vaginally delivered neonates.
